# Assembly card

`@asm` + indented instructions; no block punctuation or instruction strings needed. Optional header qualifiers: `volatile`, `inline`, `goto`.

```c
@f add5(int x) int
  int y
  @asm
    movl %[src],%[dst]
    addl $5,%[dst]
    out [dst] "=&r"(y)
    in [src] "r"(x)
    clobber "cc"
  y
```

Example targets x86. NanoC forwards instructions to the target assembler unchanged. Each raw instruction gets a newline; quoted C strings are accepted verbatim too. Optional sections, once each, in this order:

| Word | Payload |
| --- | --- |
| `out` | C output constraints, e.g. `"+r"(x), "=m"(memory)` |
| `in` | C input constraints, e.g. `"r"(x), "i"(42)` |
| `clobber` | Changed registers, `"cc"`, `"memory"` |
| `labels` | C jump labels; requires `@asm goto` |

Supports named operands, fixed-register constraints, matching operands, early clobbers and compiler attributes through ordinary C. Emits `__asm__`; requires a GNU-assembly backend (GCC/Clang tested). Instruction set, ABI and dialect belong to the target compiler (e.g. `-masm=intel`). `volatile` retains side effects; `"memory"` is a compiler barrier, not a hardware fence. [Backend contract](https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc/Extended-Asm.html).
